commands.intent: Report which repositories track a real environment file and which only ship an example
aliases: which repos have env files committed
do any of my repos track a .env

params.name: --owner
params.description: GitHub login; defaults to config.json defaultOwner

params.name: --include-forks
params.description: include forks, which are excluded by default

commands.notes: Separates a tracked .env from a .env.example plus a gitignore rule, which is the same convention working correctly. Shallow clones, because code search misses dotfiles and throttles.

commands.intent: List the repositories of an owner whose name matches a pattern
aliases: give me repos containing playwright in name
which repositories have X in the name

params.name: --pattern
params.description: case-insensitive regex matched against the repository name

params.name: --owner
params.description: GitHub login; defaults to config.json defaultOwner

params.name: --include-forks
params.description: include forks, which are excluded by default

commands.notes: gh search repos matches description and README too, so it answers a different question; this filters on the name itself.

commands.intent: Sweep every repository of an owner for credentials that look real
aliases: do any of my repos contain secrets
scan my github for leaked keys
find hardcoded api keys and tokens
secret leak audit across my projects

params.name: --owner
params.description: GitHub login; defaults to config.json defaultOwner

params.name: --contextual
params.description: also report low-confidence keyword hits, which are usually test data

commands.notes: Vendor-prefixed tokens are reported as high confidence; keyword-plus-literal hits are suppressed unless asked for. Files whose job is to detect secrets are suppressed separately. Working tree only at clone depth 1 - git history is not scanned.
